findings.title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: The `getResourceName` method handles the USERS resource type (returning 'All users' for the type resource, or the username for specific user resources), but does not handle the newly added CLIENTS resource type. When a policy has resourceType 'Clients', the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. For the type-level resource this returns 'Clients' which is acceptable, but for specific client resources (whose name is the client's internal ID/UUID), it will return the raw UUID instead of the human-readable clientId. This will result in poor UX when displaying which resources a permission applies to in the admin console.

findings.title: canMapRoles does not check admin roles, inconsistent with canManage
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManage(ClientModel)` first checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` before falling back to permission evaluation, but `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only check for explicit permissions without any admin role fallback. This means a user with the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role can update/delete clients but cannot map their roles unless a separate MAP_ROLES permission is explicitly granted. In V1, having MANAGE_CLIENTS implicitly allowed role mapping. This inconsistency may cause unexpected authorization failures for administrators who have the MANAGE_CLIENTS role but no explicit fine-grained permissions.

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is never called
findings.body: The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` at line 262 is defined but never invoked anywhere in the class. It appears to be leftover code from a previous design for `canExchangeTo`, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. This dead code should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Unused static import TOKEN_EXCHANGE
findings.body: The static import `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` on line 46 is never referenced in the class. The `canExchangeTo` method that would have used it now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

findings.title: Arrays.asList used for single-element list in hasPermission
findings.body: In both `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 225) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 250), `Arrays.asList(scope)` is used to create a single-element list that is then checked with `contains()` inside a nested loop. Since there's only one expected scope, this could be simplified to a direct `scope.equals(s)` comparison (as done in `hasGrantedPermission` at line 279), avoiding the unnecessary list allocation and contains() overhead on every permission evaluation.

findings.title: Event listener guard only checks V1 feature flag, may cause UnsupportedOperationException if both V1 and V2 are enabled
findings.body: The event listener is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1 flag). If both V1 and V2 features are enabled simultaneously, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients().setPermissionsEnabled()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. This would cause an unhandled exception during client removal events. The guard should either also exclude V2 (`!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)`) or the V2 implementation should handle `setPermissionsEnabled` gracefully (e.g., as a no-op instead of throwing).
